title: Explicit matroids with exponentially large extended formulations
formal: Editorial algorithmic-explicitness variant: does there exist a uniform deterministic polynomial-time independence test defining matroids \(M_n\) on [n] for all n≥1, and constants c>0,n0, such that the linear extension complexity of each base polytope satisfies \(\operatorname{xc}(B(M_n))\ge2^{cn}\) for all n≥n0?
definitions:
A matroid on [n] is a nonempty hereditary family I of subsets with the exchange property: if U,V belong to I and |U|<|V|, some e in V minus U has U∪{e} in I. Bases are its inclusion-maximal independent sets. The base polytope is the convex hull in R^n of their zero-one incidence vectors.

Explicitness means one deterministic Turing algorithm, given n in unary and the n-bit incidence vector of S, decides S∈I_n in time at most a fixed polynomial in n. There is no external independence oracle or nonuniform advice. This selects a stronger, concrete interpretation of the source’s word explicit.

A linear extended formulation is a finite system of real linear inequalities and equations defining a polyhedron Q in any finite dimension, together with an affine map whose image is B(M_n). Extension complexity is the minimum number of inequalities; equations do not count, and coefficients may be arbitrary real numbers. The lower bound must apply to every such extension, irrespective of coefficient bit length or construction algorithm. Linear refers to linear inequalities, not a bound linear in n.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked construction, proof of the matroid axioms and uniform polynomial independence test, and exponential lower bound on all extensions, or prove no family meeting these requirements exists. Nonconstructive counting and a family whose membership requires unbounded search do not meet the chosen explicitness condition.
context: Nonconstructive arguments yield matroids with exponential extension complexity. Ferroni and Schröter emphasize the unresolved explicit-family problem and discuss a candidate whose explicit determination is itself difficult.
why: This asks for concrete exponential extension-complexity obstructions where counting already proves existence.

import_provenance.original_title: Explicit matroids with exponentially large extended formulations
import_provenance.original_statement: Construct an explicit family of matroids on n elements whose base polytopes require 2^{Ω(n)} inequalities in every linear extended formulation. Counting proves such matroids exist, but does not identify a concrete family.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Editorial continuation of Kaibel’s work on compact formulations for structured matroid classes; the 2025 paper explicitly records the contrasting explicit-family question as open.
